Hook Site Plan

Port Hook was the port district of a far larger Ancient city. This page reads your site plan back, sets the Ancient city beside the one players will find, places the hamlets and camps of its environs, and fits the plan onto the scale model's ground at 1:1. Everything here is proposed. The questions at the end are the decisions that are yours.

The Ancient city's limits, about 10 km across.

Readings I added (check them)

  1. The freeway's south half crosses the drowned downtown. The way in is a ramp at its south end, then the deck east and north to a Freeway Gate where the wall meets the ring. I have the west arc fallen, so that this stays the one clear approach; standing, it would reach the walled ground too.
  2. The wall is drawn as a later work, not the Ancients': the Ancient city was open. Who built it is question 3.
  3. The Hykkousoi village sits in the drowned downtown's west, outside the wall and reached only by water, open to the sea: that is what makes it the smugglers' haven.
  4. "Density and height fade the further we get from the downtown": the Ancient towers are graded by distance from the downtown's centre, not from the port (M1 graded them from the port).

The Ancient city and the city today

Both maps are drawn in your sketch's frame. The north arrow is true north for the recommended placement on the ground (B, below). The tower marks are a sample of the Ancient blocks on the port's own 130 m grid, sized by height; they show density, not final positions.

On Hook's ground, at 1:1

Your sketch fitted onto the scale model's ground round Hook (5.1), with the spit as it stands today. Yellow is the sketch's land over today's water, which would have to be raised. Red is today's land under the sketch's water, which would be drowned or cut. Blue is the sunk downtown. Only the ground inside your city limits is counted; past them the coast stays natural.

PlacementLand keptTo raiseDepth raised (median, 90th percentile)To drownPort Hook
B, turned 34°16.5 km²14.0 km²8 m, 128 m3.6 km²kept as built
A, north up13.9 km²16.7 km²26 m, 147 m6.0 km²re-laid on a new coast

B is the recommendation. It keeps Port Hook as built, needs less new land and drowns less. The wall lands on the spit's east end, and the drowned downtown on today's lagoon, which is already 1 to 10 m deep.

the hard part In both placements the north ridge runs into the open sea, where the water reaches 130 to 150 m. As drawn it is a 3 km ridge rising from deep water. It could be shortened to the shelf, or its outer half could be an Ancient mole (question 2). The rest of the raising is shallow: the mainland strip east of the wall, and the south-west strip, both under about 10 m.

The reshaping would be Hook's own landform records, as the spit is: outlined benches in core/world (today's change), queued for the scale model.

What carries over, what is redone

Kept

  • Port Hook as built (with placement B).
  • M1's machinery: the port's grid continued, stable ids from the lattice, core/tags records, the ruin-state field, the node test with negatives.
  • Outlined landforms in core/world (natural outlines, a held quay edge, fill-only shelves).
  • The site editor's whole-city square (?ext=7000).

Redone

  • The ruin's extents and field: height and density by distance from the downtown's centre; the drowned half; the freeway with its fallen arc; the wall and its gates.
  • The landforms: the Alexandria plain, strait and drowned shelf from earlier today are dropped, the spit's outline reworked.

New

  • Thirteen places as core/hamlet and core/camp records.
  • The ring freeway on kits/ancient-transit (an elevated highway, ruin states by span).
  • The wall: a kit to build it from (question 3 decides whose style).

Your answers

  1. Placement: B. The plan turned 34° so its waterfront lies on today's quays; Port Hook stays as built.
  2. The north ridge: as drawn. The full length into water 130 to 150 m deep, its flanks steep; the hill and Lantern Point on it.
  3. The wall: the Pirate Emperors'. Raised from Ancient rubble against raids from the jungle side, repaired by Voth, held by the Izani now.
  4. The freeway's west arc: fallen. The south ramp and the east arc to the Freeway Gate are the one clear approach.
  5. The Drowned Spire: one Spindle standing to its crown, the village in its upper floors, pods on the crown.
  6. The bay is Port Hook's harbour, the Hook breakwater kept as built (the proposal's default).
  7. Names stay working names until the tongues give the real ones (the proposal's default).

Next: S1, the ground for placement B, then S2, the records.
